name: fix_shell_report_path_traversal
description: read_report.sh concatenates an unvalidated filename onto a base directory with no traversal check -> canonicalize with realpath -m and verify the result is still inside the base dir; incomplete-fix broken only rejects a name that STARTS WITH "../", missing the equally-effective escape via a real subdirectory ("subdir/../../secret.txt")
prompts: read_report.sh takes one argument, a report filename, and prints its contents by running `cat "$base/$name"` where base is the reports/ directory - with no validation that the resulting path actually stays inside reports/. A name containing ".." path segments (however they're arranged - a leading "../", or a real subdirectory followed by enough ".." to climb back out and further) can read arbitrary files elsewhere on the filesystem. Fix read_report.sh so any name that resolves to a path outside reports/ is rejected (print an error to stderr and exit non-zero), while a name that resolves to a real file inside reports/ (including inside a subdirectory of reports/) still prints its contents exactly as before.

setup_files.read_report.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Print the contents of a report file named $1, which must live inside the
# reports/ directory.
# VULNERABLE: $1 is concatenated onto the base path with no validation at
# all, so a name containing ".." segments can escape reports/ entirely.
base="reports"
name="$1"
cat "$base/$name"

test_setup_files.test_traversal.py:
import os
import subprocess

os.makedirs("reports/subdir", exist_ok=True)
with open("reports/q1.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Q1 revenue: 42\n")
with open("reports/subdir/note.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("just a note\n")
with open("secret.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("TOP SECRET DO NOT LEAK\n")


def run(name):
    return subprocess.run(["sh", "read_report.sh", name], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)


# normal read still works
r1 = run("q1.txt")
assert r1.returncode == 0, f"normal read failed: exit {r1.returncode}, stderr={r1.stderr!r}"
assert "Q1 revenue: 42" in r1.stdout, f"unexpected output for normal read: {r1.stdout!r}"

# leading ".." traversal must not leak the secret
r2 = run("../secret.txt")
assert "TOP SECRET" not in r2.stdout, "leading-../ traversal leaked the secret file"

# the same escape via a real subdirectory (not just a leading "../" prefix)
# must ALSO not leak - this is the case a naive "starts with ../" check misses
r3 = run("subdir/../../secret.txt")
assert "TOP SECRET" not in r3.stdout, "subdir-prefixed traversal leaked the secret file"

print("PASS")

reference_solution.read_report.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Print the contents of a report file named $1, which must live inside the
# reports/ directory. Any name that resolves outside reports/ (via ".."
# segments, however many levels deep) is rejected.
base=$(cd reports && pwd)
name="$1"
target=$(realpath -m "$base/$name")

case "$target" in
    "$base"/*)
        cat "$target"
        ;;
    *)
        echo "invalid path" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
